text:
ryan: Hey — saw a 3x KV warmup latency spike in the mistral-7b dedicated pool starting around ~1862345600. Started after the tokenizer PR landed. Peaking p95 token latency went from ~45ms -> ~150ms for short chat messages.

sara: Is this across the whole pool or one host? Any change in batch shapes?

ryan: Entire pool. We rolled the tokenizer change that enables byte fallback for some weird control chars. Batching shifted: more single-request batches. Byte-fallback hits jumped to ~18% from 2%.

mina: Byte-fallback increase + more single-item batches smells like kernel picker swapping to a slower kernel often while KV is cold. Can you paste kernel-picker logs and a short pprof sample?

ryan: Pasting snips — kernel-picker shows a lot of small requests taking the "byte_fallback" execution path, and kv-cache warmup spikes: 

```
[2026-11-03T12:34:10Z] req id=abcd kernel=fast_gemm est_tokens=12 batch=1 -> chosen=byte_fallback reason=token_bytes>threshold
[2026-11-03T12:34:10Z] req id=efgh kernel=fast_gemm est_tokens=8 batch=1 -> chosen=byte_fallback reason=token_bytes>threshold
kv_cache_warmup: 2.1ms -> 20.7ms (p95)
pprof: cpu: 120ms samples 
  45% runtime/kernel_byte_fallback
  30% kv_cache_lookup
  12% tokenizer/byte_map
```

alex: What does your batch size histogram look like? If we're getting many batch=1 calls the per-request overhead + kernel choice can dominate.

ryan: hist (last 10k reqs): 
```
batch_size: {1: 62%, 2: 18%, 3-8: 15%, >8: 5%}
avg_tokens/request: 9.3
byte_fallback_rate: 18% (was 2% before)
```

perf-bot: Automated alert: p95 token latency increased 3x for mistral-7b pool. Trace: https://perf.redwood/trace/1862345678 (canary link) :warning:

sara: Quick canary idea: force the kernel picker to prefer the fast_gemm path for a small percent of traffic (canary 5%) or temporarily disable byte_fallback to see delta. If latency drops, we know fallback path is the main cost.

mina: Also check kv warmup policy: our prefetch TTL and kv_warmup_threshold may be too aggressive for single-request batches. If the kernel path causes a slightly different KV key shape (e.g., kv_dim mismatch) we can thrash the cache. Look at model metadata: num_heads, head_dim, kv_dim, rope_scale.

ryan: Ran the canary (5% force fast_gemm). Results: median token latency down 30%, p95 down 60% on canary slice. Disabling byte_fallback entirely dropped p95 to near baseline. Numbers: 
```
control p95: 150ms -> canary p95: 65ms -> disable-fallback p95: 48ms
byte_fallback_slice p95: 210ms
```

alex: That strongly implicates byte fallback kernel being expensive for small batches. Why did byte fallback rate jump? Could be tokenizer inserting extra invisible chars or an extra BOS/EOS token in some chat templates. Also check if the tokenizer PR changed replacement/unicode handling.

ryan: Good catch — found that one chat template concatenates a user-provided string without trimming leading \uFEFF on copy/paste. Sample prompt: `\uFEFFUser: hi\nAssistant:` triggers fallback. Once stripped, tokenization goes back to normal.

mina: Two follow-ups: 1) Fix prompting trimming & sanitization in SDK to reduce accidental byte fallbacks. 2) Update kernel-picker heuristics to consider token_byte_rate and small-batch penalty: simple heuristic patch below.

```
// pseudo
if (token_byte_rate > 0.1 && batch_size <= 2) {
  prefer_kernel = fast_gemm; // avoid byte_fallback for tiny batches
}
```

mina: Also double-check model metadata conversion for this mistral checkpoint — earlier we saw a kv_dim transposition bug that made the runtime pick the slower KV code path. Verify `num_heads=32, kv_dim=64` match runtime expectations.

sara: Agreed. We'll push three changes: prompt sanitization in devex, a temporary kernel-picker heuristic tweak, and a model-metadata validation job. I'll own the job, @ryan can you open the validator PR?

ryan: On it — creating a small canary PR to sanitize inputs + a kernel-picker flag for 5% canary. Follow-up: run longer 24h canary to ensure no regen quality regressions.

perf-bot: Deploy scheduled: canary=5% kernel-picker-flag on mistral-7b pool at 1862345900, owner=@ryan :rocket:

alex: Thanks team — good find. Once SDK sanitization and validator land, we should see byte_fallback back to baseline and KV warmup spikes disappear.

ryan: Thanks — I'll paste follow-up numbers after the 24h canary. :thumbsup:
